_comment: Generated by build/manifest.py from src/*.lua. Do not hand-edit -- the function definitions in src/ are authoritative, this is derived. natives.json (see tools/dump_natives.py) is the companion catalogue of the raw engine surface.

tiers.easy: Ess.Easy.* -- guardrails. Intent-named presets, smallest surface, hard to misuse.
tiers.core: Ess.* -- named parameters and full control. The bulk of the framework.
tiers.raw: Ess.Raw.* -- the primitives the other tiers are assembled from.

Ess.AIOrders.command.description: along in vehicles on its own (see BEHAVIORS.follow below for the confirmed setup sequence)

Ess.AIOrders.setGroup.description: / .group(name) -> guids A standalone stand-in for ContractFramework's `inst.groups` -- lets `attack`/`follow`/`enter` target ANOTHER named group without needing a contract instance to hold the registry.

Ess.Atmosphere.blending.description: is a region blend running RIGHT NOW

Ess.Atmosphere.set.description: set one or many values in ONE transaction, which matters: the fade duration is a property of End(), so separate transactions mean separate fades and a visibly staggered result.

Ess.Atmosphere.setColor.description: colour channels are 0..255 and alpha defaults to 255, matching every corpus call site.

Ess.Bones.attachFX.description: -call recipe: read the bone's world position, spawn the FX there, attach it to the bone, then snap its transform exactly onto the bone so it doesn't drift before the next tick.

Ess.Bones.detachFX.description: -op, not an error) so callers don't need their own nil-guard around cleanup.

Ess.Bones.probeNames.description: -name sweep: builds every `prefix..suffix` combination, pcall-probes Object.GetHardpointPosition for each, and returns the hits (as {name=, x=, y=, z=}) plus how many candidates were tried in total.

Ess.Bones.waitForReady.description: CONFIRMED GOTCHA: a freshly Pg.Spawn'd model's hardpoints return nil for ~0.3s after spawn -- reading them synchronously at spawn time silently fails.

Ess.Camera.beginCinematic.description: enters cinematic mode and blends in.

Ess.Camera.blend.description: (re)arm the blend time so the NEXT placeCamera eases to its new spot over nDur seconds instead of cutting.

Ess.Camera.endCinematic.description: release control back to the player and stop any watch/orbit follow loop.

Ess.Camera.fade.description: Graphics.Effect.CameraFade (0=clear, 1=black) -- a THIRD distinct native table, see below .lookAtObject(uGuid, bone, i) / .lookAtPoint(x,y,z,i) / .hold(i) / .endCinematic(i) / .panicRevert()

Ess.Camera.followHardpoint.description: -ops: re-read the hardpoint's world position every `interval` seconds (default 0.05) and push it straight into Camera.SetPosition.

Ess.Camera.fov.description: / .restoreFov(i, nDuration) CONFIRMED (wiki/namespaces/graphics.md): Graphics.Camera.SetFovParams(nCameraIndex, nAngle, nDuration) / RestoreFovParams(nCameraIndex, nDuration) -- blends the field-of-view to a new angle over nDuration seconds, then reverts.

Ess.Camera.lookAtAnchor.description: -ops on this engine until an active Camera.SetLookAt binding exists -- not even a hardcoded oversized test teleport moves the camera without one.

Ess.Camera.lookAtObject.description: lock the camera onto an object (optionally a specific bone/ hardpoint).

Ess.Camera.lookAtPoint.description: lock the camera onto a fixed world point (coord form).

Ess.Camera.panicRevert.description: force-release EVERY active cinematic (the always-works escape hatch; the lua-bridge still accepts commands while control is locked, so this can be fired blind to recover).

Ess.Camera.placeCamera.description: put the cinematic camera at a fixed world vantage.

Ess.Camera.stopShake.description: for the "ConstantlyRandom" preset takes the player INDEX directly, NOT a camera guid (see below)

Ess.Cinematic.define.description: register a reusable cutscene under a name.

Ess.Cinematic.play.description: steps = { {type=, <params>, hold=}, ... }   (see STEP handlers below for each type's params) opts  = { camera=(true, take over the screen), blend=(0, instant cuts), skippable=(true), skipKey=(0x1B ESC), startFade=(false, open on black), i=(0 player index), onDone=fn(ctx) } Each step fires in order; the timeline advances `hold` seconds after firing it (hold 0 / omitted = fire the NEXT step the same tick, so several actions can start together). A {type="wait"} step just holds. ALWAYS restores camera/control on finish, skip, or stop -- a cutscene can never strand the player. Skippable: pressing ESC fast-forwards -- every remaining step still FIRES (so mission actors that a cutscene spawns/positions all end up in place), just with zero holds.

Ess.Cinematic.skip.description: fast-forward the active cutscene (drain remaining steps instantly)

Ess.Cinematic.stop.description: end it now, restore control, run onDone

Ess.Color.hsv.description: h in [0,360), s and v in [0,1] -> rgb (rainbows, distinct tints)

Ess.Color.lerp.description: blend two { r, g, b } colours, t in [0,1] (health-bar gradients)

Ess.Color.of.description: look up a preset by name ("red", "orange", ...)

Ess.Contract.Accept.description: Ess.Contract.Abort()  Ess.Contract.Status()  Ess.Contract.List() ContractFramework.lua's own version was only ever a stub placeholder (`C.UI = C.UI or {}`, never implemented -- "need a .gfx; see README"). Reusing Ess.UI here instead of hand-rolling a second widget implementation is the whole point of absorbing uilib first.

Ess.Contract._applyRelations.description: ---- relations: now a two-line wrapper over Ess.Relations, replacing the ~25-line hand-rolled snapshot/apply/restore pair this file used to carry independently.

Ess.Contract._run.description: run ONE objective as its own task; onDone(true|false) reports its outcome (exactly once)

Ess.Contract._runList.description: Run an objective LIST in a mode ("sequential" default | "parallel"), calling onDone(true|false) once the whole list resolves.

Ess.Contract._spawnUnits.description: spawn def.units, bucket their guids by group, and track them for teardown (one task bucket).

Ess.Contract._startBackground.description: background conditions running for the WHOLE contract: an overall time limit, plus any def.fail conditions (protect a target / stay in an area).

Ess.Contract._startSupport.description: ---- support + AI orders + triggers runner (from _startBackground; one auto-cleaned task bucket) ----

Ess.Easy.AIOrders.guard.description: "guard" is the friendlier name for the "defend" behavior -- hold an area, fight anything inside it.

Ess.Easy.Airstrike.at.description: ---- Easy presets: a jet pass plus a few shells on a spot / your target / your own head ----

Ess.Easy.Camera.fadeOut.description: / .fadeIn() -- named presets for the two confirmed values, no 0/1 to remember.

Ess.Easy.Camera.orbit.description: smoothly orbit a target (radius/height/speed/startAngle) chase + orbit DAMP the follow through Ess.Vec.lerp by DEFAULT (jitter-free on a fast subject) -- pass smooth=false for the old exact-snap, or smoothFactor (0..1, higher=snappier) to tune the damping.

Ess.Easy.Camera.watch.description: watch a target (e.g. a heli you spawned) fly in; default = static locked shot, opts.chase = follow from opts.angle

Ess.Easy.Cinematic.play.description: the zero-opts entry (skippable cutscene, camera takeover).

Ess.Easy.Cinematic.shot.description: build one static camera shot on a world point, held `seconds`.

Ess.Easy.Confirm.description: pop a yes/no dialog; onNo is optional (default: do nothing).

Ess.Easy.Console.open.description: browse the full registry, grouped by namespace.

Ess.Easy.Console.search.description: typed substring filter (name/usage/desc, case-insensitive) over the registry; re-opens the board with only the matches.

Ess.Easy.Debug.overlay.description: toggle the overlay on/off (call again to hide). opts (all optional): x, y (screen pos), interval (refresh s, default 0.2), radius (nearby scan, default 40), i (player index). Returns the panel, or nil when toggled off.

Ess.Easy.Followers.orderEnter.description: role defaults to "driver" (not AIOrders' own "passenger" default) specifically so a lone follower enters as the one seat that keeps every LATER order (move/attack/guard/...) working through the SAME guid already on the roster.

Ess.Easy.Followers.recruit.description: follows the local player (Ess.Player.character(0)) with the confirmed default distances (see 60_aiorders.lua's BEHAVIORS.follow).

Ess.Easy.Followers.showMarkers.description: / .hideMarkers() -- named aliases for the boolean toggle, see Ess.Followers.setMarkersEnabled's own header for what they actually turn on.

Ess.Easy.Fun.dance.description: make your character do the "technoviking" dance.

Ess.Easy.Fun.fanfare.description: play the mission-success (or, with false, mission-fail) music sting.

Ess.Easy.Human.giveWeapon.description: spawn-free "just give them a gun by name"

Ess.Easy.Impulse.knockback.description: shove uGuid directly AWAY from fromGuid (default source = you) with a slight upward lift -- the "the blast sent them flying" feel.

Ess.Easy.Impulse.launch.description: pop something straight UP (a hop, or a big launch).

Ess.Easy.Impulse.speedBoost.description: a forward SPEED BOOST (the Spy Hunter effect).

Ess.Easy.Mark.enemy.description: radar+PDA, no world icon -- matches WaveDefense's real convention (don't clutter the world with icons for every enemy).

Ess.Easy.Mark.objective.description: all three surfaces -- matches ContractFramework's convention for a real mission objective.

Ess.Easy.Mark.zone.description: world ring only -- the ground-disc "go here" case, no radar/PDA clutter.

Ess.Easy.Menu.description: opens immediately, one flat level, no bools/tables to configure.

Ess.Easy.Objective.clear.description: POLLS the area's population and completes when every `faction` unit in it is dead -- the "eliminate the enemies here" goal the engine has no clean per-kill event for. Shows "N left".

Ess.Easy.Objective.destroy.description: that object dies (marks it on radar/PDA/world)

Ess.Easy.Objective.reach.description: enter the radius (drops a "go here" ground ring)

Ess.Easy.Objective.survive.description: completes after N s; FAILS if the player dies

Ess.Easy.Player.freeSupport.description: ignore all airstrike/support stock + unlock requirements, so you can call any support for free.

Ess.Easy.Player.ghost.description: stealth mode: drop your AI detectability to the engine's own floor so AI perception (mostly) can't see you; call again (or pass false) to restore your original value exactly.

Ess.Easy.Player.giveAllRewards.description: dispense every unlock reward at once.

Ess.Easy.Player.unlockFastTravel.description: unlock every landing zone so you can fast-travel anywhere.

Ess.Easy.Relations.makeAllies.description: every pair within the list becomes mutually allied.

Ess.Easy.Relations.makeHostile.description: every faction in the list becomes hostile to PMC.

Ess.Easy.Relations.war.description: make two factions fight EACH OTHER (mutually hostile), independent of the player.

Ess.Easy.Spawn.airstrike.description: call a shell down on your own head (a classic sandbox gag).

Ess.Easy.Spawn.crate.description: a supply drop that parachutes down just in front of you.

Ess.Easy.Spawn.enemies.description: drop a squad of hostiles a short way in front of you and set them ON you: an instant firefight in one line.

Ess.Easy.Spawn.explosion.description: a big boom ~10 units in front of you (in front, not on your face, so it's dramatic without instakilling).

Ess.Easy.Spawn.fx.description: an effect at a world location.

Ess.Easy.Spawn.weapon.description: drop a weapon PICKUP on the ground in front of you (walk over it to grab it).

Ess.Easy.Squad.orderTeamFollow.description: returns just this team to following (vehicle-aware, same smartFollow dispatch as Ess.Followers.order("follow", ...) -- see that file's header).

Ess.Easy.Squad.queue.description: named-callback-only shorthand over Ess.Squad.queue; use Ess.Squad.queue directly for onCancel or per-step timeouts.

Ess.Easy.Squad.setFormation.description: follows the local player in "wedge"/ "column"/"line"/"diamond" at Ess.Squad.setFormation's own default spacing.

Ess.Easy.Vehicle.summon.description: spawn a vehicle in front + hop in the driver seat -- the whole "give me a <vehicle>" thought in ONE line

Ess.Easy.World.clearWanted.description: instantly lose all heat (clear the pursuit/wanted level)

Ess.Easy.World.freezeTime.description: stop the day/night cycle -- THIS ONE IS RELIABLY MAP-WIDE

Ess.Easy.World.noPursuit.description: one call: stop the current chase AND keep new organic heat off (true/nil = on; false = restore normal pursuit behavior) ceiling back up -- a bigger n, a (faction, n) form, 99, SetPursuitLevelTimes, SetCustomPursuit were ALL tried and none undo it; only a save-load or full restart resets it. capLevel() therefore logs a loud warning every call -- it's a real capability ("this mode never exceeds heat 2") but it is a session-length commitment, not a tunable. pursuit (despite the names) and do NOT block a scripted .start() -- they only gate ORGANIC (AI- driven) escalation. The off switch for a live chase is .clear(), nothing else.

Ess.Easy.World.removeMapBoundary.description: drop the invisible walls fencing the player into the unlocked map

Ess.Easy.World.resetAtmosphere.description: undo any tint/brightness back to the region default own atmosphere preset override it; see the note at the impl

Ess.Easy.World.setTimeSpeed.description: rescale the cycle (0 = frozen); no getter exists to restore it

Ess.Easy.World.tint.description: wash the world in an ambient color (0..255)

Ess.Easy.World.unlockTimeOfDay.description: release the lock; leaves the clock where it is unless given

Ess.Event.on.description: getting the shape wrong doesn't error, it just silently never fires, so double-check against wiki/namespaces/event.md if a handler seems dead.

Ess.Followers._followLoopAnchorOf.description: the disposable TinyGeometry a vehicle-escort/ on-foot-resume loop is currently repositioning every tick for this guid (nil if not in one right now).

Ess.Followers.order.description: command the whole roster -- any of AIOrders' 11 behaviors

Ess.Followers.setMarkersEnabled.description: opt-in floating world markers, see below

Ess.Gfx.setVisible.description: KNOWN BUG THIS FIXES: the getter is `GetVisible()`, not `IsVisible()` (which doesn't exist -- calling it nil-calls and gets silently swallowed by pcall, so nothing visibly breaks, it just never toggles).

Ess.Hud.Faction.hide.description: hide one meter. The real teardown, since RemoveMeter is a no-op.

Ess.Hud.Faction.inZone.description: mark the player as inside that faction's territory, which is how the game highlights the relevant meter as you cross a border.

Ess.Hud.Faction.pursuit.description: the red "you are being hunted" gauge.

Ess.Hud.Faction.restoreLevels.description: undo .levels(), back to the game's own vocabulary `function ShowAll(oWidget, nDuration) end`). An Ess.Hud.Faction.show existed here briefly and was withdrawn on measurement: it reported success and the meters still vanished, because there was never any code behind it.

Ess.Hud.banner.description: a clean, icon-free, centered text banner via the EventFanfare "custom" trick (CONFIRMED live-tested)

Ess.Hud.clearMessages.description: wipe the message box, visible AND queued.

Ess.Hud.hint.description: the native tutorial-style hint popup (icon+sound), stays up until hidden -- CONFIRMED reusable for arbitrary text, live- tested with a screenshot (wiki/snippets.md)

Ess.Hud.image.description: put an image in an objective-tray slot (add/set/timer/pursuit/inZone/hide/show/levels) (MessageBox reads `self.sName` to pick its widget), and Hud.SubtitleBuffer is literally the same functions bound to a table with a different sName. A dot-call silently targets the wrong widget or errors. Every call in this file uses a colon. "all players", which is what you want in singleplayer. Do NOT pass it explicitly to the Tutorial functions -- see Ess.Hud.tutorial's note, they are broken for that case in the shipped script. They are callable and return nil, so nothing tells you at runtime. Not wrapped here.

Ess.Hud.location.description: the region-name banner ("Playa del Este"-style card)

Ess.Hud.message.description: a message-box line; returns a handle for update/remove

Ess.Hud.objective.description: set the persistent objective-tray line (nil clears it); nSlot defaults to 1 (the "current objective" line)

Ess.Hud.radio.description: a transient radio-chatter subtitle that auto-clears after nHold s

Ess.Hud.resources.description: show (for nDuration seconds, default 3) or hide the cash+fuel readouts.

Ess.Hud.suppressResources.description: the game's own "hide these during a cutscene" switch, separate from show/hide and independently settable per counter.

Ess.Hud.title.description: the stylised animated title overlay, the nicest-looking text primitive the game has.

Ess.Hud.tutorial.description: the tutorial strip -- STICKY, pass nil to clear

Ess.Hud.updateMessage.description: edit a message that is still QUEUED (see the caveat below)

Ess.Human.allowCorpseCleanup.description: keep a body for a scene

Ess.Human.carrying.description: hauling a body/crate (blocks climb, swim, most weapons)

Ess.Human.persistTransform.description: pin the character's current position/orientation so the engine stops re-deriving it.

Ess.Human.refillAmmo.description: the confirmed "set to GetMaxReserveAmmo" one-liner, independently duplicated across pmccon001.lua/vzacon001.lua

Ess.Human.setJostle.description: stop crowds shoving a placed NPC

Ess.Human.setState.description: Upright|InVehicle|Subdued|Cower + "Idle"/clip NO feedback on a bad state -- see impl note

Ess.Impulse.mass.description: the mass getter, surfaced at the Core tier too.

Ess.Impulse.spin.description: an OFF-CENTER impulse to make something roll / flip (spyhunter's barrel roll).

Ess.Input.clear.description: flush the pending key-event ring buffer

Ess.Input.held.description: is this key down RIGHT NOW (no buffer drain)

Ess.Input.hijackController.description: niche -- see caveat below; low priority to verify further, most mods don't need this

Ess.Input.poll.description: -> bool } The ONLY correct input-polling shape on this engine: Loader.PopKeyEvents() (an edge-triggered ring buffer -- each byte is a VK code that went up->down since the last drain) for discrete presses, PLUS Loader.GetKeyboardState() (a 256-byte snapshot) for "is this held right now." Call this ONCE per tick and read both fields off the result.

Ess.Input.usingController.description: Gui.ControllerInUse -- for branching HUD hint text ("Press A" vs "Press E"), the common case

Ess.Keys.on.description: key = a VK number (0x74) OR a name ("F5", "space", "a", "1", "up") -- fn(bShift)

Ess.Keys.vk.description: resolve a name to its Windows VK code (the map this uses)

Ess.Layers.begin.description: open a mode: snapshot baseline + gate saves. false if already open.

Ess.Layers.expect.description: Declarative convergence: make the world match { present = {...}, absent = {...} }, issuing only the minimal add/remove.

Ess.Log.description: prefixed Loader.Printf, used by the rest of Ess

Ess.Loop.list.description: the shape a dashboard/monitor wants to poll on an interval and just render.

Ess.Loop.start.description: tickFn() returns true to keep going, false/nil to auto-stop

Ess.Loop.stats.description: safe to hold onto and print without it changing under you.
Ess.Loop.stats.returns: { interval, ticks, lastDuration, avgDuration, lastError } | nil

Ess.Loop.stop.description: cancels a running loop early; its next scheduled tick will see it's gone and quietly not reschedule (no error, no dangling reference).

Ess.Mark.clear.description: tears down every surface a handle actually used, plus the zone anchor prop if there was one.

Ess.Mark.object.description: opts: radar=true, pda=true, world=true (floating icon), disc=false (ground ring), kind=, rgb=, radius= (disc), discAlpha=, size=/dist= (floating-icon size + draw-distance)

Ess.Mark.zone.description: opts: world=true (ground ring), radar=true, pda=true, icon=false (ALSO a floating icon), kind=, rgb=, discAlpha=, size=/dist= (floating-icon size + draw-distance)

Ess.Math.approach.description: move `cur` toward `target` by at most `maxStep` (a frame-rate-independent ease when maxStep = speed*dt).

Ess.Math.dist2DSq.description: squared distances -- skip the sqrt when you only COMPARE ("which is closer", "is it within r").

Ess.Math.lerpAngle.description: interpolate angle a -> b (DEGREES) the SHORTEST way, so 350 -> 10 eases +20 through zero, not -340 the long way round.

Ess.Math.pointAhead.description: -- project (x,z) forward by a yaw (spawnAhead math)

Ess.Math.remap.description: linear rescale: map v from [inLo,inHi] onto [outLo,outHi] ("a 0..maxHealth into a 0..1 bar," "a distance into an alpha").

Ess.Math.within2D.description: is the second point within radius r of the first, on the ground plane? The `dx*dx + dz*dz <= r*r` range test, named -- no sqrt, no way to fumble the squaring.

Ess.Math.wrap.description: wrap v into the half-open range [lo, hi) -- keep an index, an angle, or a cursor in-band.

Ess.Minimap.autoZoom.description: retune the auto-zoom instead of defeating it modules declare bare globals and the engine's import() machinery namespaces them, so it is really MrxGuiBase.MinimapDataUpdateHandler. construction (`self:SetEventHandler("GuiMinimapUpdate", MinimapDataUpdateHandler)` at mrxguibase.lua:1445), so it holds the original regardless of what the module table says afterwards.

Ess.Minimap.lockRange.description: set it and KEEP it, by replacing the auto-zoom handler

Ess.Minimap.range.description: set the view range once (see the stomp warning below)

Ess.Minimap.show.description: hide or show the whole minimap.

Ess.Minimap.widget.description: the widget itself, for anything not wrapped here.

Ess.Object.faceObject.description: same, but face another object's CURRENT position.

Ess.Object.fadeOut.description: fade an object out over nDuration, then DESTROY it.

Ess.Object.hasLabel.description: Labels: a free-form string tag the engine and other scripts read (e.g.

Ess.Object.isAttachedTo.description: is uGuid attached to uOther specifically?

Ess.Object.kill.description: Ess.Object.kill / .remove -- both one-way per the Object namespace's own notes: Kill destroys (leaves a corpse/wreck), Remove deletes the object outright.

Ess.Object.localToWorld.description: full 3D local->world (incl. pitch/roll -- use over Ess.Math.rotateOffset when the object may be tilted)

Ess.Object.moveToObject.description: teleport uGuid onto uTarget's position in one call.

Ess.Object.revive.description: confirmed with an optional delay second arg (e.g.

Ess.Object.setName.description: makes it findable via Ess.Guid / allByName

Ess.Object.size.description: model bounding-box extents (takes a GUID, not a name)

Ess.Object.snapToGround.description: drop (or lift) the object so it sits on the terrain, optionally hovering nOffset units above it.

Ess.Object.spawnAhead.description: spawn in front of the player (hides the yaw->sin/cos "in front of me" trig a beginner won't know; tOpts.useView=true places it where you're LOOKING, not body-facing)

Ess.Object.speedSq.description: scalar speed. One native call (Object.GetVelocitySquared) + a sqrt.

Ess.Object.stopAllAnimation.description: stop every animation channel at once.

Ess.Object.vehicleOf.description: -> vehicle guid (driver OR passenger) or nil.

Ess.Shop.isOpen.description: the short one is NOT a convenience -- it is for the game's own catalogue. _SetupShopFlash only renders an item if it has sDesc AND sTexture AND nCurrentStock, or if its sId is found in MrxSupportData.tSupportData. A short-form item with an id the game does not know renders NOTHING, with no error. Ess.Shop always uses the full form, and requires sDesc/sTexture, so this cannot happen. tCallbackData, appends the item's sId and the quantity, and unpacks the lot. Passing no callback data -- which is what this wrapper does -- makes the signature simply fn(sId, nQuantity). Same trap as Create refuses if an entry exists. So a shop left open blocks every later one. Ess.Shop.open closes any existing shop first rather than failing. with Escape was measured to leave the player WITH NO GAME CONTROL: the buy and close callbacks all fired correctly and the shop deregistered itself, but input never came back. See Ess.Shop.close, which exists as much to recover from that as to close a shop -- calling it when nothing is open is a valid, supported rescue. one. It pops the focus queue, then only reassigns ControlModeManager[uOwner] IF THERE IS A NEXT HOLDER -- so draining the queue to empty leaves the mode flag stuck at its previous value. Measured: queue depth 0, holder nil, mode still `true`. Anything in Ess that takes control focus and is the last holder inherits this, so reach for Ess.Shop.close's repair rather than rediscovering it.
